Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows marked elevation of the right hemidiaphragm with a smooth contour and no evidence of pleural effusion or subdiaphragmatic mass, which is characteristic of unilateral diaphragmatic paralysis (often due to phrenic nerve palsy). The "scalloping" on the left likely represents normal diaphragmatic undulations or eventration, but the primary pathological finding explaining the right-sided elevation in this context is paralysis.
